hook: A *Bisleri* water sample failed two labs; FSSAI now prosecutes
hook_b: A *Bisleri* water sample failed two labs; FSSAI now prosecutes
tldr: Food regulator FSSAI sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International after a packaged drinking water sample was declared unsafe.

beats.what: The first sample breached bromate limits; on the company's appeal, the referral lab also declared it unsafe after detecting PAHs.
beats.why: FSSAI has stepped up enforcement this year against food businesses, e-commerce firms, energy drink and alcoholic beverage makers.
beats.care: Bottled water is a daily buy for many; the report doesn't say which batch or city the sample came from.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: FSSAI also sanctioned prosecution against Vasant Masala, Tit-Bit Foods India, Mimansa Industries and Asha Confectionery.

cards.q: Do you check the label or batch on bottled water before buying?

qs: Which batch and city was the sample from?
How often are packaged water brands tested?

facts.t: FSSAI suspended the licences of *2* firms: Urmi Lifesciences and Gaur Ayurvedic Store.

viz.verdict: Two labs called the sample unsafe; bad for buyers' trust

learn.t: FSSAI = Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, the national food regulator

watch: Prosecution will proceed under the FSS Act, 2006; Asha Confectionery has been ordered to recall chocolate-filled cookies.

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.title: FSSAI orders prosecution against Bisleri International for unsafe packaged drinking water

fact: FSSAI orders prosecution of Bisleri after its water sample failed *2* labs
twist: The referral lab found polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), on top of the first lab's bromate failure.
